whyThisExists: Distilled from two untracked interrupted-run artefacts held by three abandoned worktrees. Landing the 22.5 MB pair was rejected - the 10 MB log carries machine-local absolute paths this repo forbids committing, and both are regenerable residue of a run that completed 1 of 904 species. NOT calling it regenerable either: the already-landed 3.5 KB population census (BCU2.12-full-run.json) contains zero occurrences of "error", "fail" or "reject", so the failure census below was recorded nowhere at integration and would have died with the worktrees.

reDerivation.parseRule: Count a row as a name-collision failure when its done[<nodeId>].detail matches field 'name' ('<name>') is already used by another commander effect. Group by the quoted <name>. Everything else with a detail is grouped by that detail with quoted strings, digit runs and node ids masked.
reDerivation.command: python -c "import json,collections,re;d=json.load(open('tree-language.ledger.json'))['done'];c=collections.Counter(re.search(r"field 'name' \\('([^']*)'\\)", r.get('detail') or '').group(1) for r in d.values() if r and r.get('detail'));print(len(d), sum(c.values()), c.most_common(10))"
reDerivation.classifyingRule: A number in this fragment is a dated reading of one interrupted run, never a contract. Do not pin it in a guardrail and do not quote it as a steady-state rate.

population.denominatorNote: The obvious reading - failures over all rows - is wrong by a third, because a row carrying a non-null `record` is a COMMITTED node and belongs in neither numerator. 10,164 rows committed, 5,433 did not, out of 15,597.

finding.headline: Corpus-wide node-name uniqueness has no deterministic fallback. Of 15,597 attempted node subjects this run committed 10,164 and failed 5,433 (34.8%), and 3,633 of those 5,433 failures - 66.9% of all failures - are the SAME defect: a name-collision gate the model-only repair loop cannot satisfy.

gate.behaviour: rejects when draft['name'] is in context['takenNames']
gate.defect: the message hardcodes "another commander effect", but this call site checks PASSIVE-TREE NODE names - every one of the failures above logged a message naming the wrong subject kind, which is why the ledger reads as 984 distinct shapes until the quoted name is masked out

caller.seeding: taken_names is seeded corpus-wide from the ledger own committed node record.name values (run.py:1084) and grows as records are accepted

repairBudget.behaviour: the only recovery is another model call; there is no deterministic rename fallback on this path

existingDeterministicCounterpart.note: the items pipeline solves the identical corpus-wide name-collision problem deterministically, keeping the lexically first id of each collision group and renaming every other row. The node path has no equivalent, which is the asymmetry this finding is about.

logFailuresClassifiedAsTransient.verdict: all retried transport/model-transient conditions, not corpus findings - the reason the 10 MB log is not owed work

stillLiveAtIntegration.verdict: both code sites are still present, so the finding is OPEN work, not a closed incident
